chartTokens.description: Shared series colors, light and dark themes, and supporting styles for charts, legends, and related controls.
chartTokens.paletteBody: Seven global slots run through theme blue, cyan, amber, green, violet, light gray, and red. The first five colors serve comparison series. Chart-6 is neutral for unknown, unused, or unassigned states; chart-7 is danger red for errors, failures, or abnormal states. Chart colors remain independent of brand tokens.
chartTokens.slot1: Theme blue; the default primary series
chartTokens.slot6: Light gray neutral; unknown, unused, or unassigned states
chartTokens.slot7: Danger red; errors, failures, or abnormal states
chartTokens.layersBody: Global variables define the palette, Tailwind aliases expose utilities, and ChartConfig maps business series names to variables within a chart instance. Marks and legends share the same slot rather than maintaining a separate page palette.
chartTokens.globalUsage: Theme-provided colors read by CSS, SVG, and chartColor(1–7).
chartTokens.utilityUsage: Exposes bg-chart-1, text-chart-1, fill-chart-1, and stroke-chart-1 utilities with opacity modifiers such as /20.
chartTokens.instanceUsage: Generated by ChartContainer from ChartConfig and scoped to its data-chart container; this is not another global palette.
chartTokens.identityBody: Assign explicit colorIndex values to fixed series and use slots 6 and 7 explicitly for neutral and danger states. Stable ID fallbacks for dynamic entities use only the first five comparison colors. Pass the same resolved color to marks, legends, gradients, and related sliders. Slots may repeat; retain every label, value, and detail.
chartTokens.priority: chartSeriesColor resolves a valid colorIndex, then an adapted legacy category color, then a stable ID hash. Invalid runtime indices in chartColor fall back to slot 1. Legacy gray maps to slot 1; chartLegacyColor is a compatibility helper and does not read Badge HEX values. Explicit external color and theme overrides remain supported.
chartTokens.structureBody: Chart-6 represents neutral states with explicit data meaning; grids, text, and unassigned tracks retain structural tokens. Stroke and fill share a series color; opacity and component parameters control emphasis. There are currently no separate global chart-fill, chart-stroke, or chart-grid variables.
chartTokens.gridUsage: chartTrendPreset uses border with a 3 5 dash pattern.
chartTokens.axisUsage: ChartContainer renders tick labels with fg-subtle.
chartTokens.textUsage: Values and center text use fg-default; legend labels use fg-muted.
chartTokens.trackUsage: SegmentedBar and DonutSummary use muted; a track is not a data series.
chartTokens.radiusUsage: The container, each data segment, and the remainder track use sm, 4px by default.
chartTokens.gapUsage: Visible segments use half the base spacing, 2px by default; zero and unknown segments consume no gaps.
chartTokens.tooltipUsage: Floating surface, border, and floating shadow, with foreground tokens for text.
chartTokens.focusUsage: Shared charts and interactive legends use focus-ring.
chartTokens.parameters: TimeSeriesChart currently uses strokeWidth = 2 and fillOpacity = 0.12. DonutSummary defaults to an 80% innerRadius. These are component parameters rather than additional global style variables. Business charts may adjust them through existing APIs while retaining Chart Token colors.
chartTokens.segmentedGeometry: Horizontal segmented bars share SegmentedBar: the container, each data segment, and the remainder track use rounded-sm, with gap-0.5 spacing (2px by default). Gaps reveal the surface background. Available width after spacing is allocated proportionally to actual values; zero and unknown segments consume no gaps. Radius and spacing reuse existing design variables without adding chart-specific variables.
chartTokens.statusBody: Charts can explicitly use chartColor(6) for neutral states and chartColor(7) for errors or danger states. chartStatusColors and existing domain status mappings remain independent. Resource status and metric distributions currently use the fixed mapping below.
chartTokens.resourcesBody: The donut and legend in resource-status-all-01 share a category mapping with the bars in resource-metric-list-01. Existing tone identities remain stable when inputs reorder. The list's legacy neutral field maps to the cyan unknown category.
chartTokens.maintenanceBody: The source repository defines manual color values only in packages/ui/src/tokens/semantic-tokens.mjs. Edit the seven Light / Dark pairs and regenerate tokens and Registry artifacts; do not edit generated app/globals.css directly. This page reads the same source definitions.
chartTokens.consumerBody: Consumer projects can override --chart-1 through --chart-7 after the installed theme, with separate light and dark values. Retaining variable names and component references updates marks, legends, and related controls together. The following code shows the current defaults and Tailwind aliases.
